robodebt:
The Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme, led by Commissioner Catherine Holmes, found responsibility lay with the ministers who approved and defended the scheme and with senior public servants.
Scott Morrison took the proposal to Cabinet as Social Services Minister in 2015, and Alan Tudge oversaw the 2016 rollout as Human Services Minister.
Jordan Sample said the commission found the scheme was "a crude and cruel mechanism, neither fair nor legal".
sports-rorts:
Bridget McKenzie, as Minister for Sport, approved the Community Sport Infrastructure Program grants in the lead-up to the 2019 election, and the Auditor-General found the funding decisions favoured marginal and targeted seats.
Casey Example said the Auditor-General found the minister's office "ran a parallel assessment process" that did not follow Sport Australia's merit scores.
Bridget McKenzie resigned from Cabinet in February 2020 after a review found she had breached ministerial standards over a grant to a club she belonged to.

pay:
**A federal backbencher’s base salary is $239,270 a year**, for senators and members alike, since 1 July 2025. Ministers and other office holders receive an additional percentage of base on top, from 3% to 160% for the Prime Minister.

**Salaries as at 19 October 2026.** Each is the parliamentary base salary of $239,270 plus the loading of the post held, as a percentage of that base. Federal parliament only.

| Post | Loading | Salary a year |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Senator or member with no other post | none | $239,270 |
| Prime Minister | 160% | $622,102 |
| Deputy Prime Minister | 105% | $490,503 |
| Treasurer | 87.5% | $448,631 |
| Leader of the Opposition | 85% | $442,650 |
| Cabinet Minister | 72.5% | $412,741 |
| Speaker of the House of Representatives | 75% | $418,730 |
| President of the Senate | 75% | $418,730 |
| Minister outside Cabinet | 57.5% | $376,850 |
| Deputy Leader of the Opposition | 57.5% | $376,860 |
| Assistant Minister (Parliamentary Secretary) | 25% | $299,088 |
| Shadow Cabinet Minister | 25% | $299,090 |
| Shadow Minister outside Shadow Cabinet | 20% | $287,130 |

The base salary over time: $207,100 from 1 July 2018; $211,250 from 1 July 2019; $217,060 from 1 July 2022; $225,750 from 1 September 2023; $233,660 from 1 July 2024; $239,270 from 1 July 2025.

Coverage: These are salary entitlements set by the Remuneration Tribunal, **not payslips**. They leave out the electorate allowance ($39,700 to $57,100 a year), expenses, superannuation and any outside income. Committee chairs and deputy chairs are paid a further 3% to 16% that is not counted, because the Parliamentary Handbook gives no dates for who chaired what.
identity: Penny Wong's recorded party is Labor.
vote: The Senate defeated the Coalition amendments to the National Anti-Corruption Commission Bill 2022 on 29 November 2022, 28 ayes to 36 noes.
why:
The National Anti-Corruption Commission was established to give the Commonwealth a standing body able to investigate serious or systemic corruption, after years of debate about gaps in federal integrity oversight.
Jordan Sample said the commission would investigate "serious or systemic corruption across the Commonwealth public sector", including ministers and their staff.
The Albanese Government had promised it at the 2022 election, and the commission began operating on 1 July 2023.
what-happened:
In 2018 the Commonwealth bought the Leppington Triangle, land near the Western Sydney Airport site, for $29.8 million, and the Auditor-General later found it paid about ten times its value.
Casey Example said the Auditor-General found the land "was worth about $3 million".
The purchase was referred to the Australian Federal Police, and the Infrastructure Department official who led the negotiation later left the department.

accountability-robodebt:
The cited sources do not name a person or office as responsible.

The Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme found the scheme was a crude and cruel mechanism, neither fair nor legal, and that the government of the time continued to raise debts despite warnings.
Robin Example said the former government "knew this scheme was unlawful and it kept going anyway".
Morgan Sample said the department's warnings about income averaging were ignored by the ministers who kept defending the scheme.
accountability-blame:
The Auditor-General found the Minister for Sport's office ran a parallel assessment process, and the approved grants did not reflect Sport Australia's merit scores.
Jamie Example said the minister "pork-barrelled sports grants into marginal seats".
accountability-decided:
The cited sources do not name a person or office as responsible.

Casey Sample said on 30 September 2020 that the Auditor-General found the department did not conduct appropriate due diligence before it bought the land.
Taylor Sample told the Senate the then minister must have signed off on the purchase.
robodebt-live-r100:
The Royal Commission found that the Scheme was approved by Cabinet and proceeded without the legislative change to support averaging which DSS had said was needed.

The Royal Commission into the Robodebt Scheme was established on 18 August 2022, and its final report is dated 7 July 2023.

Its reports make 57 recommendations, and 47 hearing transcripts are held, which are evidence rather than findings.

The Royal Commission concluded it was a costly failure of public administration, in both human and economic terms.
